findings.criterion: Approved slice sections 5.1, 6, 10, and 11 require selective recalculation integrated with workflows/UI, visible/deferable impact authority, a representative researcher path, and a usable downstream handoff; T03 criterion 1 requires the user to compare and restore a prior adjudicated output.
findings.finding: The approved user/control path is not vertically integrated. The implementation stops at internal Python services and repositories, so a researcher cannot obtain the governed preview, enqueue controlled recalculation, compare versions, defer while retaining visibility, or restore through the production Core API/desktop boundary.
findings.reproduction: Search production Core API composition, routes/models, generated clients, and desktop controls for SelectiveRecalculationService, dependency-impact composition, preview/recalculation/restore operations, and version comparison. Only internal modules/tests and an unrelated /projects/restore route are present.
findings.requiredRemediation: Compose the smallest project-scoped production Core API contract and approved existing UI/workflow surface that makes preview, deferral, enqueue, version comparison, and restore usable with strict projections and accessible state handling. If the approved experience cannot support this without a governed reference change, stop at that real gate or replan explicitly; do not silently defer the accepted criterion.

findings.criterion: Accepted human judgments and human-gate authority must be exact, auditable, and preserved across restore/restart; T03 criterion 1 authorizes restoration only as a user decision.
findings.finding: Restore treats caller-supplied actor_type='human' plus any non-null actor_id as explicit human authority. It does not prove an authenticated principal or bind the exact completed human decision and consequence that authorize restoration.
findings.reproduction: Replace the canonical restore event actor_id with a fresh arbitrary UUID while keeping actor_type='human'. SelectiveRecalculationService.restore accepts the command and appends an adjudicated revision.
findings.requiredRemediation: Require a Core-minted authenticated actor and exact completed S04 human-decision authority (or an equivalently strong signed/transactional decision receipt), bound to project, target/prior/current revisions, operation/run/snapshot, consequence, and idempotency/CAS state. Add spoof, wrong-assignee/role/project, stale-decision, replay, restart, and concurrent-current-revision denials.

findings.criterion: Approved slice section 7 requires recalculation to re-evaluate current rights/egress policy; repository and provenance authority must prevent substituted or stale rights decisions.
findings.finding: Neither candidate admission nor restoration binds rights_status to a current policy decision. A candidate may supply any syntactically valid status, while restore blindly copies the prior adjudicated revision's status, including one less protective than current policy/current state.
findings.reproduction: Change only draft.rights_status in an otherwise admitted canonical SQLite candidate; commit/replay succeeds. Inspect repositories.py:1748-1771 and selective_recalculation.py:500.
findings.requiredRemediation: Bind the exact current policy/rights decision and its version/fingerprint within atomic enqueue, candidate commit, and restore transactions. Reject stale, substituted, or protection-relaxing authority and prove allowed-to-denied, denied-to-allowed, policy-change-between-plan-and-commit, restore, replay, restart, and rollback cases.

findings.criterion: T02 criterion 1 and selected slice decisions require truthful distinction of direct/transitive/conditional/non-material dependencies, deterministic safe cycles, and accurate user-visible cause/impact authority.
findings.finding: Cycle groups are computed from every traversed edge, including non-material edges and conditional edges explicitly decided as ignore. A non-propagating edge can therefore close a false strongly connected component and assign cycle authority to outputs that are not in a material propagation cycle.
findings.reproduction: Use source-to-A direct, A-to-B direct, and B-to-A as either non-material or conditional with disposition ignore. Both previews report A/B as a cycle group. The ordering is visible at dependency_impacts.py:395, 402, 418, and 478.
findings.requiredRemediation: Build SCC/cycle authority only from edges that actually propagate under the immutable graph snapshot and applicable recorded conditional decision. Add intersection fixtures for non-material and ignored closing edges, true conditional-propagate cycles, mixed cycle exits, stable IDs, bounds, persistence/restart, and downstream scheduling.

The selection head also stops before the declared state candidate and omits later verification-control changes from the stated range.
findings.reproduction: Replay the recorded verify.py selection from f56d16070637147177c05c3406b5669eb1707cf0 to 43d572dd8a0a0fdbb90b009ffb51ab15a591b385, then replay to bc9441a23faa1df44f80a823f432ca5988e394d6 and compare unknownPaths/rules.
findings.requiredRemediation: Regenerate the integration evidence against the exact remediation state candidate, truthfully disclose unknown-path fallback, and attach the exact selection result. Include the benchmark/profile/quality-scope changes in the affected range. Replay prior findings plus incremental boundaries only.

Under the repository's risk-selected review policy, this is not by itself an additional S05 acceptance finding, but it is not waived: preserve the disclosure, retain an exact failure inventory/report when available, reconcile the additional error, and pass the complete foundation/release matrix at W1 exit.

residuals.item: The dependency-impact benchmark measures the pure in-memory planner with an all-material SCC oracle and conservative initial thresholds; it does not measure SQLite batch/coalescing, paged persistence reads, crash/restart latency, or cross-machine release behavior.
residuals.disposition: Accepted only as initial slice characterization. Representative persistent/cross-capability budgets and regression thresholds remain mandatory at W1 exit.
